## Purpose and Public Entry Points
Nano-vLLM is a lightweight, offline Python inference engine modeled after vLLM. It loads supported Hugging Face-style model weights, batches text-generation requests, and returns sampled completions. The public API is exposed through `nanovllm/__init__.py` and `nanovllm/llm.py`; usage and benchmark entry scripts are `example.py` and `bench.py`.

## User-Facing LLM Facade
`nanovllm/llm.py` owns the synchronous `LLM.generate` interface. It accepts prompts and `SamplingParams`, constructs engine requests, repeatedly advances inference until completion, and formats output text. `nanovllm/sampling_params.py` defines generation controls such as temperature and maximum output length.

## Engine Orchestration
`nanovllm/engine/llm_engine.py` is the central coordinator between request lifecycle, scheduling, cache allocation, and model execution. It manages active sequences and progresses them through prefill and token-by-token decode. `nanovllm/engine/sequence.py` represents request state, including token history and generation progress.

## Continuous Batching and KV-Cache Lifecycle
`nanovllm/engine/scheduler.py` selects runnable sequences and forms each execution batch, separating admission/prefill needs from decode work. `nanovllm/engine/block_manager.py` allocates, reuses, and frees token blocks for attention KV cache; this is the key prefix-caching and memory-management boundary. Scheduler decisions must remain consistent with sequence state and available cache blocks.

## Model Execution Runtime
`nanovllm/engine/model_runner.py` turns scheduled sequences into tensors, invokes the model, manages KV-cache-backed execution, and returns logits or sampled next tokens. It is the boundary between engine-level Python objects and GPU tensor/model operations. Runtime behavior is configured through `nanovllm/config.py`, including model, cache, tensor-parallel, eager/compiled, and CUDA-graph-related settings.

## Model and Layer Stack
`nanovllm/models/qwen3.py` implements the supported Qwen3 transformer architecture. Core compute primitives are organized under `nanovllm/layers/attention.py`, `nanovllm/layers/linear.py`, and `nanovllm/layers/embed_head.py`; attention consumes and updates the KV cache, while the embedding/head path converts tokens to hidden states and logits. `nanovllm/layers/sampler.py` applies sampling policy to logits.

## Model Loading and External Dependencies
`nanovllm/utils/loader.py` loads local pretrained model weights; model acquisition is expected outside the engine, typically from Hugging Face repositories such as Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B. Execution depends materially on PyTorch and CUDA-capable GPU infrastructure, with optional tensor parallelism, `torch.compile`, and CUDA graphs described by the project. `nanovllm/utils/context.py` provides distributed/runtime context used by parallel execution paths.
